messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a good wash (soft cloth, mild soap, no harsh chemicals). Tune it to standard tuning (E‑A‑D‑G‑B‑E) so buyers can hear its true tone. | A clean, well‑tuned instrument looks cared for and lets buyers hear its best sound. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the body, neck, headstock, strings, and any unique features (inlay, finish, hardware). Use natural light and a neutral background. | Great photos attract more views and reduce the chance of buyer hesitation. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local music‑store listings. Note price ranges for similar models, ages, and conditions. | Knowing the market helps you set a realistic price and avoid over‑ or under‑pricing. | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | Include:
• Brand & model
• Age (or year made)
• Condition (new, like new, used, minor wear)
• Any accessories (case, strap, picks)
• Reason for selling
• Contact info | Transparency builds trust and reduces back‑and‑forth questions. | | **5. Choose Your Platforms** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments, global reach.
• **eBay** – auction or fixed price, large audience.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local music stores** – consignment or direct sale. | Different platforms reach different buyers; use a mix for maximum exposure. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target price to allow room for negotiation. For example, if you want $300, list at $350. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point keeps you from underselling. | | **7. Offer Shipping Options (if online)** | Provide free shipping for local pickup, or include a shipping cost estimate. Use a sturdy case or padded bag, and ship with tracking. | Shipping details reassure buyers and protect both parties. | | **8. Be Responsive & Safe** | Reply promptly to inquiries. Meet in a public place or arrange a video call if possible. If shipping, use a reputable carrier and keep receipts. | Good communication builds confidence; safety measures protect you from scams. | | **9. Negotiate Wisely** | Decide your lowest acceptable price beforehand. If a buyer offers less, politely counter or accept if it meets your minimum. | Staying firm on your bottom line prevents you from selling too cheaply. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | Once agreed, send a receipt or confirmation. If shipping, package securely and ship immediately. If local, hand over the instrument and collect payment in cash or a verified digital transfer. | Proper paperwork protects you and gives the buyer peace of mind. | ### Quick Tips - **Highlight Unique Features**: If your guitar has a special finish, custom inlay, or upgraded electronics, mention them. These can justify a higher price. - **Mention Maintenance History**: If you’ve had it professionally tuned or repaired, note that. It signals care. - **Use “For Sale” Tags**: On social media, tag relevant groups (e.g., “Acoustic Guitar Sale”) to increase visibility. - **Consider Trade‑Ins**: Some local music shops offer trade‑in credits toward new gear—great if you plan to upgrade. ### Example Listing (Reverb) ``` Title: 2015 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition Description: - Brand: Yamaha - Model: FG800 - Year: 2015 - Condition: Like new – no scratches, no cracks - Features: Solid spruce top, nato/okume back & sides, 0.45mm strings - Accessories: Hard case, strap, picks - Reason for selling: Upgrading to a 12‑string Price: $350 (Negotiable) Photos: [Attach 5–6 high‑resolution images] Contact: [Your email] / [Phone] ``` Feel free to adapt this template to your own guitar’s specifics. Good luck with the sale!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "How can I sell my acoustic guitar?" They want advice on selling an acoustic guitar. We can provide steps: research market value, clean it, take photos, list on platforms (eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, Reverb, local classifieds), set price, describe condition, shipping options, safety tips, etc. Also mention potential for trade-in, consignment, or local music stores. Provide suggestions for pricing, negotiation, and maybe mention using the tune_instrument function? The function is about tuning instruments, not selling. So we don't need to call it. Just give advice.
